key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with tuned DDFW parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, and deep learning can predict tensile performance from process settings.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical path to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive manufacturing by linking joint design and process optimization.
method: L18 orthogonal array experiments on AA2024-T351 DDFW
Compared friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, geometry, and friction time
Trained deep learning models to predict ultimate tensile strength
evidence_signal: The best condition achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, while the ensemble residual network reached the highest prediction accuracy with R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The dataset appears limited to a designed experimental campaign, so model accuracy and the optimal settings may need validation on broader materials, geometries, and production conditions.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
